page: Microsoft Azure D96s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, providing 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which accelerate vector and matrix operations. In benchmark evaluations, the D96s_v7 demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded performance, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 105,569.39 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 556.8 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance falling into the average category.

Memory performance is characterized by strong read-only bandwidth, reaching 7,051.06 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 345.73 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. The server exhibits top-tier throughput in static web serving at 124.31 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 152.07 million operations per second. For database operations, the PassMark database benchmark registers a strong score of 32,067.02.

Large Language Model (LLM) inference benchmarks show strong prompt processing speeds across various model sizes, including 2,647.08 tokens/sec for a small 135M model and 33.21 tokens/sec for a large 70B model. However, text generation speeds are average, dropping to 3.65 tokens/sec for the 70B model, reflecting the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration. This hardware profile is suited for multi-threaded enterprise workloads, static web serving, Redis caching layers, and database operations requiring high vCPU density and balanced memory allocation.
